scope: B06 sparse catalog metadata and B10–B14 current refresh, artwork, cache invalidation and read recovery

method.application: Current production renderer/preload and actual source-bundled main, JellyfinService, native media, protected storage and localhost HTTP. Fresh dummy-account profiles; hidden muted native windows. Shared Keychain/provider responses substituted, external fetch blocked and scheduled timer stopped after startup. Zero provider calls.
method.catalog: Fixture has20,000 songs and2,000 albums with two libraries; this run selects Archive. It is a behavior check, not an actual-library performance benchmark. A single fixture playlist supplies read-only list/detail cache changes; no playlist mutation is performed.
method.refresh: Prime song inspector, album metadata/tracks and playlist list/detail caches. Change controlled server song names, facets and image revisions plus album/playlist metadata. Actual Refresh library updates the visible song and facets while retaining search/selection and the playing duplicate queue. Revisiting song, album and playlist data reads the new values. A second journey preserves active Rock/Archive/search and selection, confirms new facet data and actual HTTP filter propagation, and retains its paused queue.
method.artwork: Real native images decode using new own-art, album-art and song album-art fallback revision tags. Both old and new resource URLs are observed through the actual proxy/image path. No visual comparison of a live server cache is claimed.
method.failures: Controlled503 reads cover song refresh, facet refresh, album metadata, cached album tracks, cached album list, and new uncached song/album queries. Loaded rows/tiles/facets and the paused queue remain available; completed read failures expose explicit Try again. Recovery reads succeed after removing the fault. An uncached failure is not mislabeled an empty library; a successful empty reply then shows the honest no-matching state. Normal read retry policy is unchanged.
method.albums: Metadata is requested by ID even with no tracks. A metadata-only failure leaves tracks usable; native Play album actually starts the ordered ten-track queue. The first track lacks title, artist, duration and other optional metadata, shows Untitled song/Unknown artist in table/player and advances real native WAV playback. Its playback does not depend on successful album metadata. Empty tracks disable album Play while metadata remains visible.
method.state: Refresh/read failures preserve the named active radio opt-ins, queue and playback intent. Music continues through healthy cache refresh; fault-recovery scenarios retain a deliberately paused queue. Only the explicit Play album action replaces the queue. No read/refresh initiates preparation.
method.cleanup: All three final driver commands terminate zero; owned native closes check absence of captured fatal output. Every owned localhost server stops and its control file resets.

fixtureCorrections: The first driver used exact song-title button names, but their accessible names also contain the artist. Scope actual song-name buttons by visible title and artwork-bearing playlist tiles by their text. The corrected complete journey passes without a production change.

The owned catalog adapter includes the real AlbumArtists read route used by current album search, a read-only playlist response and explicit read faults. The original/base server is retained for the first two journeys; the extended server adds only flags used by the final read-recovery journey.
limits: Controlled dummy account/server and muted native WAV. No live Jellyfin metadata/artwork timing or large-library performance claim.
Playlist results cover read-cache freshness only, not mutation permissions, cross-client writes or uncertain-write recovery.
No deferred smaller/enlarged checks. Observed listener comprehension, VoiceOver, audible quality, broader OS/hardware coverage and the earlier Q10 shutdown diagnostic remain open.
